topic: Two ears, one mouth: Harvard's follow-up question study and the Stoic founder who predicted it

story.title: Zeno of Citium silences a young chatterbox in Athens
story.who: Zeno of Citium, founder of Stoicism

quotes: The reason why we have two ears and only one mouth is that we may listen the more and talk the less.

facts.claim: To a young man who was talking nonsense, Zeno said we have two ears and only one mouth so that we may listen more and talk less
facts.source: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of the Eminent Philosophers 7.23, trans. R. D. Hicks (1925)

facts.claim: Across live conversation studies, people who asked more questions, especially follow-up questions, were liked more by their partners; responsiveness explained the effect, and people did not predict it
facts.source: Huang, Yeomans, Brooks, Minson & Gino, It doesn't hurt to ask: Question-asking increases liking, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 113(3), 2017

facts.claim: In the speed-dating study, people who asked more follow-up questions were more likely to get agreement for a second date (a later reanalysis disputes this study's statistics)
facts.source: Huang et al., Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 2017, Study 3

beats.headline: WANT THEM TO LIKE YOU MORE?
beats.voice: Want people to like you more? Talk less. Harvard proved it. A Stoic called it first.

beats.headline: Askers were liked more
beats.voice: Strangers chatted. Some were told to ask lots of questions. Their partners liked them more.

beats.headline: Follow-ups won second dates
beats.voice: Follow-up questions worked best. Speed daters who asked more got more second dates.

beats.headline: A young man won't stop

beats.headline: Speak one part in three
beats.voice: A follow-up proves you heard. That is what people remember.

beats.voice: Your challenge today: in your next conversation, follow up twice before you say a word about yourself.

beats.headline: FOLLOW FOR STOIC POWER
beats.body: Think like Plato. Speak like a leader. Influence like a CEO.
beats.voice: Follow to think like Plato, speak like a leader, and influence like a CEO.

reel_caption:
Want people to like you more? Ask, then ask again.

In 2017, Harvard researchers (Huang, Yeomans, Brooks, Minson and Gino) found that people who ask more questions are liked more. Follow-up questions did the most work. Speed daters who asked them got more second dates.

Zeno of Citium said it around 300 BC. A young man in Athens wouldn't stop talking, so Zeno told him we've got two ears and one mouth to listen more and talk less. It's in Diogenes Laertius, Lives 7.23.

If you've been searching how to be more likable, here's the cheapest answer zeno stoicism gives you: let them talk, and prove you heard.

I'm trying it today. Follow up twice before you talk about yourself.

Save this for your next meeting.
